title: sqlite_storage: ts as u64 cast unchecked for negative
description:
## Trigger
A negative i64 hlc_timestamp in the log_entries SQLite table (from database corruption or future tooling bug) is cast to u64 at sqlite_storage.rs line ~126 via ts as u64, wrapping to a very large timestamp value.

## Bad behavior
The log entry would appear to have a timestamp far in the future, corrupting Merkle-CRDT time ordering and potentially causing reconciliation to reject the entry as having an implausible timestamp.

## Fix
Add a guard: if ts < 0 { return Err(StorageError::Corrupt(format!("negative hlc_timestamp {} in entry {:?}", ts, id_bytes))); }. This gives a clear diagnostic on corruption rather than silent data corruption.
